intro.title: The Great Convergence — Why AI Software Development, Why Now
intro.note: Opening teaching map for Matt Weber. “The Great Convergence” is Matt's framing for the forces changing software development: capable models, agent harnesses, faster development cadence, and organizations reclaiming software that fits how they actually work.

canvasChildren.title: Welcome — I am Matt Weber
canvasChildren.note: Senior developer for a few decades; recent Angular and C# backend work; builder of open-source platform tools for exercising AI-development learning; now fascinated by teaching it. Contact: golfergeek@gmail.com.

canvasChildren.note: Code offers enormous training material and unusually fast evidence through compilers, tests, linters, and observable behavior. It is highly testable, not magically simple or perfectly deterministic.

canvasChildren.title: This requires a mind shift—and it is not for everybody
canvasChildren.note: The convergence creates an opportunity, not an obligation. “Not now” can be responsible. High-assurance systems can still use AI for research, tests, review, and bounded proposals while preserving line-by-line human authority.

canvasChildren.title: Cadence changes the developer's job
canvasChildren.note: Cadence is the sustainable rate of moving from intention to trustworthy evidence. The developer increasingly manages outcomes, boundaries, contracts, authority, integration, and proof—not merely lines of code.

canvasChildren.note: Fast generation amplifies both strong definition and weak assumptions. Agent training means maintaining the agent's operating environment: role, context, memory, standards, tools, permissions, examples, and evaluations.

Welcome — I am Matt Weber
Senior software developer for a few decades
children.note: Establish experience without turning the introduction into a résumé. The useful point is that this perspective comes from living through several generations of software practice.

children.title: Recent work — Angular frontends and C# backends
Then I discovered AI software development
children.note: Describe this as a change in the way software is conceived, delegated, built, tested, and maintained—not merely a faster autocomplete.

children.title: I built open-source platform tools to exercise what I was learning
children.note: The tools were a laboratory: build real systems, expose weak assumptions, and turn discoveries into repeatable practices.

children.title: Now I am fascinated by how to teach it
Contact — golfergeek@gmail.com
The opening premise
Software was the natural first proving ground for foundation models
children.note: Code offers enormous training material, rapid feedback, executable tests, compilers, linters, and observable outputs. It is more verifiable than many knowledge-work domains, although production software is never perfectly deterministic.

children.title: Code is unusually testable—not magically simple
children.note: A build can pass or fail and a test can pass or fail. Requirements, architecture, security, usability, and business fit still require judgment. This distinction keeps the argument credible.

children.title: The early road became visible very quickly
The adoption boundary — this is not for everybody
children.note: The Great Convergence creates an opportunity, not an obligation. “Not now” can be a responsible decision when the organization, codebase, evidence system, or risk tolerance is not ready.

children.title: This requires a real mind shift
From code production to outcome definition and evidence
From individual typing to delegated, parallel work
From static process to a maintained development system
From avoiding change to managing change deliberately
Some companies should not walk this path right now
No owner for AI risk, quality, or operating policy
No reliable test or review system
No capacity to maintain tools, context, and standards
The business value does not justify the transition cost
Some codebases demand exceptionally high assurance
children.note: Safety-critical, regulated, security-sensitive, and foundational systems may require justified confidence that each line and every interaction is appropriate.

children.title: AI assistance does not remove accountability
Generated code may require line-by-line human review
Formal controls, traceability, and independent evidence still govern
AI can still strengthen high-assurance codebases
Research and explain unfamiliar behavior
Generate candidate tests and adversarial cases
Find inconsistencies, risks, and missing documentation
Propose constrained changes for rigorous human review
Automate evidence collection without automating final authority
Adoption is a continuum—not an on/off switch
Explain and research
Suggest and review
Implement inside narrow boundaries
Run verified workflows
Expand authority only when evidence supports it

1 — Code completion

3 — Agent harnesses
children.note: Claude Code and the growing family of IDE, CLI, plugin, and agent-first environments made the model part of an operating loop.

children.title: Prompt — the immediate request
Context — repository, instructions, history, and retrieved knowledge

LLM — reasoning and generation inside the loop

What changed when the harness arrived
The unit of work became an outcome, not a completion
children.note: The developer can ask for a researched, implemented, tested, and explained change rather than accepting one suggestion at a time.

children.title: Context became an engineering discipline
What must the agent know?
What should remain durable project or organizational memory?
What belongs in code, documentation, a skill, an agent, or the current task?
Tools turned language into action
Evidence allowed the loop to continue
Build, lint, test, run, inspect, challenge, and revise

Every week improves some part of the system
Models become more capable
Context windows and usable working memory grow
Harnesses and IDEs improve orchestration and visibility
Agents work longer and recover from more failures
The four forces converging
1 — Capable foundation models
children.note: Models can understand and produce increasingly large, connected portions of a software system.

children.title: 2 — Operational harnesses
children.note: IDEs, CLIs, plugins, agent views, tools, context, skills, and sub-agents turn model capability into repeatable work.

children.title: 3 — Radical development cadence
children.note: Cadence means the rate at which a team can move from intention to evidence and then safely begin the next iteration.

children.title: 4 — Companies need software that fits
SaaS gives broad capability but rarely matches every workflow
Spreadsheets and internal stopgaps expose the remaining gaps
AI changes the build-versus-buy boundary
Organizations can selectively reclaim differentiating software
Cadence changes the developer's job
From writing every line to managing contracts
children.note: The developer increasingly defines outcomes, boundaries, interfaces, invariants, evidence, and authority. “Contract manager” is a useful metaphor, but technical judgment and accountability stay with the developer.

children.title: One developer can coordinate parallel work
Multiple sub-agents on one bounded issue
Multiple tasks progressing across one codebase
Multiple codebases open in one working environment
Humans integrate decisions, conflicts, and proof
Capable agents can implement many professional tasks
children.note: Avoid the universal claim that an agent is simply “as good as most coders.” Performance varies by task, context, tools, model, and verification. The important change is useful implementation capacity under strong supervision.

children.title: The scarce work moves
Choosing the right problem
Defining boundaries and acceptance criteria
Supplying trustworthy context
Reviewing architecture, security, and product fit
Verifying evidence and retaining organizational learning
The rhythm of software development changes
Specifications become living instruments
children.note: Teams still need shared intent. The difference is that they can test an interpretation quickly, inspect working software, and revise the specification with evidence.

children.title: Fewer meetings devoted only to expensive handoffs
More conversations about decisions, risks, and tradeoffs
Shorter loop — define → delegate → inspect → learn → repeat
Rapid iteration replaces the fantasy of perfect first-pass requirements
Taking back the software process
Not “replace every SaaS product”
children.note: Buy commodity capability when it fits. Build where workflow, integration, data, control, or differentiation makes ownership worthwhile.

children.title: Own the gaps that matter
Turn spreadsheet stopgaps into intentional systems
Keep code, decisions, skills, agents, and governance together
Make organizational learning compound in the repository
For now — business-centered development
children.note: This program concentrates on software where rapid, verified iteration can resolve concrete business friction or create measurable value. It does not use the lowest-risk business case to justify uncontrolled use everywhere.

children.title: Maintain cadence against the long-neglected backlog
Small internal workflows that never justified a traditional project
Spreadsheet and manual-process gaps
Integrations and reporting that SaaS does not quite provide
Iterate from one verified slice instead of waiting for a grand rewrite
Then pursue genuinely new company value
Internal projects — efficiency, insight, and operational fit
Customer-facing projects — service, experience, and retention
Expansion projects — new products, capabilities, and revenue
Cadence is not raw output
children.note: Useful cadence is the sustained rate of moving from business intention to trustworthy evidence. More generated code without verification is inventory, not value.

children.title: Faster development requires a stronger system
children.note: When implementation accelerates, weak assumptions and weak controls also propagate faster. Guardrails, governance, and process become more important, not less.

children.title: Guardrails
Permissions and authority boundaries
Protected data, secrets, environments, and deployment paths
Stop conditions and required human decisions
Governance
Approved models, harnesses, tools, skills, and agents
Ownership, evidence, decisions, exceptions, and review dates
Traceability from intention through implementation and proof
Process
Define → challenge → delegate → inspect → verify → learn
Independent review for consequential changes
Rollback, incident learning, and durable updates
Agent training is a maintained organizational capability
children.note: “Training” here usually means shaping the agent's operating environment rather than training a foundation model: clear roles, durable context, tools, permissions, examples, standards, and evaluation.

children.title: Each agent knows its role, outcome, boundaries, and stop conditions
Project memory explains architecture, decisions, and current constraints
Company memory explains policies, terminology, risks, and priorities
Coding standards and quality bars are explicit and testable
Skills package repeatable methods; specialized agents package responsibility
Tests and evaluations prove that instructions still work
Owners maintain the system as code, policy, and tools change
Adoption requires comfort with continuing change
AI capability and interfaces change rapidly
Models, context, tools, and agent behavior improve
Harnesses, providers, pricing, and vendor incentives move
Yesterday's workaround can become tomorrow's liability
Separate durable principles from changing terrain
Durable — intent, evidence, authority, security, ownership
Terrain — products, models, interfaces, limits, and tactics
An organization may freeze a good-enough system
children.note: That is a valid choice, but it should be conscious: stability trades away some future capability, efficiency, and safety improvements.

children.title: To benefit next week, next month, and next year
Budget for review, experiments, upgrades, and retirement
Introduce change through evidence and controlled rollout
Protect teams from novelty churn while avoiding permanent stagnation
This commitment is genuinely challenging
The organization must learn to build software again
children.note: Reclaiming software means reclaiming the responsibilities that SaaS vendors had absorbed. Generation capacity without product ownership, testing, operations, and maintenance creates a fragile portfolio.

children.title: Manage a real project portfolio
Internal projects
Customer-facing projects
Expansion projects
Prioritize by value, risk, ownership, and maintenance cost
Restore the testing habit
children.note: Many organizations stopped exercising this muscle when vendors owned most application behavior. Owning software again means proving it continuously.

children.title: Acceptance tests — does it solve the intended business problem?
Unit and component tests — do local rules hold?
Integration and contract tests — do boundaries agree?
Browser and workflow tests — can a user complete the real journey?
Security and isolation tests — who can do what to whose data?
Regression tests — did new cadence break old value?
Own operation after generation
Deployment, observability, support, incident response, and rollback
Maintenance owners and lifecycle funding
Retire software that no longer earns its cost

Speed amplifies good definition—and bad assumptions
Parallel agents amplify capacity—and coordination risk
Large context helps—but does not guarantee understanding
Green tests are evidence—not proof of product value or safety
Governance must move at the new cadence
The winning capability is a trustworthy development system
